paper.title: Efficient Online Lexicographic Generalized Low-Rank Matrix Bandits

unmapped: Matrix-valued arms X in R^{d1 x d2} with ||X||_F <= 1; parameter matrices Theta_i^* of rank at most r with ||Theta_i^*||_F <= S
Multi-objective (m objectives) vector-valued reward, each objective with its own GLM link mu_i and parameter Theta_i^*; regret measured per objective against the lexicographically optimal arm
Lexicographic trade-off assumption with known parameter w (Assumption 5)
Bounded noise |eta| <= R and bounded mean |mu_i| <= U
Existence of an exploration distribution D over the arm set with bounded second moment M of the score function and pairwise-independent rows or columns (Assumption 6)
Learner uses rank r, w, D_rr (r-th singular value lower bound), M, L_mu, U, R in tuning
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t\in[T]$, the learner first observes the arm set $\SX\subseteq\R^{d_1\times d_2}$, selects an arm $\X_t\in\SX$, and then receives a stochastic reward vector $y_t=(y_{t,1},\ldots,y_{t,m})\in\R^m$ ... $\E[y_{t,i}\mid \X_t]=\mu_i(\langle \X_t,\Theta_i^*\rangle)$

symbols.d_1: number of rows of matrix arms
symbols.d_2: number of columns of matrix arms
symbols.r: upper bound on rank of each parameter matrix

conditions: Assumptions 1-6 (low rank, ||Theta_i||_F<=S, ||X||_F<=1, c_mu<=mu_i'<=L_mu, bounded rewards U and noise R, lexicographic trade-off w, exploration distribution with score moment M)
regret bound holds for each objective i in [m_obj]
proof additionally uses sqrt(M(d1+d2)r)/D_rr <~ (d1+d2)r and treats U, L_mu, R, c_mu, S as constants
tuning: lambda_perp = c_mu T/(k log(1+c_mu T/(k lambda_0))), k=(d1+d2)r-r^2

source.label: thm:scalar_lowglm
source.quote: Suppose that Assumptions~\ref{ass:low_rank}--\ref{ass:exploration} hold. ... Then, with probability at least $1-2\delta$, for every objective $i\in[m]$, the cumulative regret satisfies $R_i(T)=\widetilde O\!\left(W^{\rm sca}\cdot(d_1+d_2)r\sqrt{T}\right)$, where $W^{\rm sca}=\sum_{i=1}^m (1+w)^{i-1}$.

results.notes: Probability 1-2delta. Regret is defined through means (pseudo-regret on the realized arm sequence) but holds w.h.p. Multi-objective lexicographic setting not fully captured by the ontology.

symbols.d_1: number of rows of matrix arms
symbols.d_2: number of columns of matrix arms
symbols.r: upper bound on rank of each parameter matrix

conditions: bound for each objective i in [m_obj]
proof additionally uses sqrt(M(d1+d2)r)/D_rr <~ (d1+d2)r and treats U, L_mu, R, c_mu, S as constants
tuning: same parameters as Theorem 1 (T_1, lambda_0, lambda_perp, S_perp)

source.label: thm:lexi_lowglm_ucb
source.quote: Suppose that Assumptions~\ref{ass:low_rank}--\ref{ass:exploration} hold, and run Algorithm~\ref{alg:lexi_ucb} with the same parameters as specified in Theorem~\ref{thm:scalar_lowglm}. Then, with probability at least $1-2\delta$, for every objective $i\in[m]$, the cumulative regret satisfies $R_i(T)=\widetilde O\left(W_i^{\rm lex}\sqrt{m}\cdot(d_1+d_2)r\sqrt{T}\right)$, where $W_i^{\rm lex} = 1+w+\cdots+w^{i-1}$.

results.notes: Online Newton-step estimator updates; O(T) total estimator update cost. Probability 1-2delta.
